# Constraint Box — what it is, what runs, and what does not

## Bottom line

Constraint Box is one directory holding two products that do not touch each other.

- A packaged Python product, `constraint_box/src/constraintbox/`, installed as the `constraintbox` CLI. It contains MiniLevOS (a deterministic flow kernel), the ClaimGate gate entry point, and the five-library formal core. It is tested and reruns clean.
- A loose set of 20 untracked scripts, `constraint_box/scripts/cb_*.py`, that run the LLM swarms and write every receipt under `constraint_box/receipts/`. None of them imports the packaged product.

`grep -rn 'import constraintbox' constraint_box/scripts/` returns only `run_external_validation.py` and `verify_wheel.py`. No receipt under `constraint_box/receipts/` mentions minilev or leviathan. The owner's one-line definition of CB — "a deterministic gating LLM constraint harness for mass looping swarms" — is answered by the scripts, not the package. The package is the deterministic kernel; the swarm loop never enters it.

Everything below separates these two, because merging them is how a claim about one gets attributed to the other.

---

## 1. What CB is and why it exists

### The owner definition

The governing statement lives verbatim at `constraint_box/docs/OWNER_RULINGS_VERBATIM_20260806.md:41`, and that file declares itself the winner over any model summary (`:3-6`). `constraint_box/docs/CB_DEFINITION_OWNER_CANON_20260806.md:14` breaks it into five load-bearing clauses:

| Clause | What it demands |
|---|---|
| deterministic gating | non-LLM code decides pass or fail |
| constraint harness | the harness restricts options, it does not score content |
| mass looping swarms | many calls, repeated, with a live-or-dead test per loop |
| diverse LLMs | more than one model family, measurably different inputs |
| LLMs don't control their own gating | the producer cannot write its own pass criteria |

The complementary ruling at `OWNER_RULINGS_VERBATIM_20260806.md:24-30`: CB "gates the domain, not the truth". CB bounds the set of answers that could be right. It never rules on whether a finding is correct.

### The failure mode it answers

Three separate failure records sit in the tree, and they agree.

1. The v3 collapse, `OWNER_RULINGS_VERBATIM_20260806.md:207-211`. Many nodes running from one shared root input returned the same answer wearing different names. A swarm that shares its input is one model with extra billing.
2. The producer-visible receipt, `constraint_box/docs/01_THEORY.md:40-46`. Five earlier ClaimGate defences were defeated the same way: the agent could see, and therefore satisfy, the criterion it was being judged against.
3. Four confirmed holes red-teamed on 2026-07-20, recorded in the docstring of `constraint_box/claimgate_plugin/claim_verify.py`. All four root in the agent authoring its own pass criteria.

### Where the answer is executable

The clearest code expression of "gates the domain, not the truth" is `gate_claim()` at `constraint_box/scripts/cb_run.py:118`. Seven deterministic members run in a fixed stack:

| Member | What it restricts | Line |
|---|---|---|
| JSON extraction | a reply that is not a JSON object is refused | `:125` |
| msgspec | strict struct, `forbid_unknown_fields` | `:135` |
| jsonschema | verdict enum {PARKED, BLOCKED, ADMIT_FOR_TESTING}, `promotion_allowed` const false, `claim_ceiling` minLength | `:147` |
| portion | confidence must fall inside a declared interval — outside is "not a possible value" | `:159`, `:162` |
| celpy | the gate rule carried as registry data, not as a branch in code | `:164` |
| icontract | precondition: confidence above 0.9 requires a ceiling of at least 30 characters | `:176` |
| SDG check | refuses causal language without a causal packet | `:185` |

Not one member scores content. The enum bounds the answer set, portion bounds admissible numbers, the ceiling requirement enforces auditability. The receipt ceiling written at `cb_run.py:299-300` states it plainly: format, shape and machinery only.

### The declared bias

`constraint_box/docs/CB_BIAS_AND_DIVERSITY_MEASURE_20260806.md:26` declares CB operationalist, nominalist, sentimentalist, and committed to no causality. Three of those four reach code. The nominalist and operationalist commitments ride the enum, range and SMT members. The no-causality commitment is carried by exactly one code site, the SDG word-match at `cb_run.py:185-189`. The sentimentalist third has no code site anywhere in the tree. It is doctrine with no gate.

### Voices as pre-language

`VOICE_MMM` at `cb_run.py:36` holds nine voices, each a single `Terms: …` vocabulary line, injected ahead of the task at `:66`. That placement is the whole mechanism — priming before generation, not a rule applied to output.

`constraint_box/docs/VOICES_AND_MMM_DIVERGENCE_MECHANISM_20260806.md:66-77` forbids CB from ever checking output for voice-vocabulary conformity, on the grounds that compliance rebuilds the v3 collapse. That boundary is held: `gate_claim` inspects JSON shape, enum membership, numeric range and ceiling length, and no voice term appears in any check. The SDG member is the closest thing in the codebase to the prohibited pattern — it is a literal word-match on output — but it enforces the bias, not voice conformity. It is the place that would erode first.

## 2. MiniLevOS

### What it is

MiniLevOS is a runtime, singular. One module, `constraint_box/src/constraintbox/mini_levos.py`, 2,596 lines, holding one `MiniLevRuntime` class. Seventeen frozen `FlowPolicy` instances ride on it inside `src/`, plus an eighteenth at `constraint_box/workers/attractor_basin_v1/basin_controller.py:1043`.

It is not a package — it is one module inside the `constraintbox` package. It is not a provider shim — `_provider_harness/` is a sibling package the kernel never imports, and the dependency runs the other way. It is not primarily a conformance contract — `leviathan_reference.py` is a separate optional observer the kernel does not depend on.

A hook returns a typed observation. The controller alone picks the next node. Every step appends to a hash-chained ledger. The run ends in one of five fixed terminals.

### What the kernel refuses, structurally

Enforced at construction time:

- only a GATE may emit RETRY (`mini_levos.py:997`)
- positive terminals (ELIGIBLE, RELEASED) are reachable only from a gate PASS (`:979-985`)
- non-retry edges must form a DAG (`:1012`)
- every node must reach a terminal (`:1017`)
- the transition map must be exhaustive per node (`:1007`)

Enforced at runtime, every step:

- hook output containing any of 34 authority key names (`verdict`, `terminal`, `next_node`, `release`, `promotion_allowed`, …, `:63-89`) is refused with controller HOLD
- hook source digest, code digest and live module binding are re-verified before and after every step (`:1872`, `:2003`)
- Python runtime identity is re-captured and compared each step (`:2004`)
- the ledger path is atomically reserved with `open("x")` plus fsync (`:1797-1823`) — an existing ledger path is refused outright

### The flow catalog

| Flow | Path | Nodes | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| formal controller | `formal_flow.py:199` | 2 | live CLI run, ELIGIBLE |
| bounded proposal retry claim | `proposal_minilev_flow.py:596` | 4 | 12 tests, callbacks are test doubles |
| Leviathan conformance analogue | `leviathan_reference.py:177` | 4 | 6 tests, direct call ELIGIBLE |
| integrated receipt lease | `integrated_minilev.py:139` | 1 | 1 test with a real expiry control |
| foreign Lev eval observation | `lev_eval_observation_flow.py:474` | 2 | 7 tests |
| 12 external-capability tool→gate flows | `external_*_capability*.py` | 2 each | not run; they dispatch engines outside CB |

### Evidence rung

Fresh rerun, six modules, 71 tests, all OK: `mini_levos` 39, `proposal_minilev_flow` 12, `lev_eval_observation_flow` 7, `execution_lease_minilev` 6, `leviathan_reference` 6, `integrated_minilev` 1. One live `constraintbox formal run` wrote a real `constraintbox.mini-levos-receipt.v1` receipt with terminal ELIGIBLE, 2 steps, ledger verification "2 record(s)". Rung: passes local rerun.

### What it conforms to

Exactly one artifact: `/Users/joshuaeisenhart/lev-main/plugins/sdlc/flows/exec-validate.flow.yaml`, the flow named `sdlc-exec-validate`. Conformance is one-directional observation of that file's text shape plus a structural correspondence to CB's own four-node analogue. CB imports no Lev code and inherits no Lev authority — Lev's `validate` node is still `op: lev.exec`, which CB refuses to treat as a gate. The one intentional divergence: Lev's timeout-then-escalate path becomes CB's deterministic HOLD, so exhaustion can never invoke a model or a human inside the flow.

`lev_eval_observation_flow.py` is the strongest structural expression of the rule. It has two nodes, no ELIGIBLE, no RELEASED, no ClaimGate, no retry, no lease. A foreign `pass` and a foreign `fail` cannot select different CB terminals.

### Declared ceilings

| Ceiling | Source |
|---|---|
| the proposal flow's callbacks are test doubles, not LLM or provider evidence | `docs/CONTAINED_CORE_PRODUCT.md:282` |
| one hook only, no heartbeat, no distributed lease, no reboot recovery, no hostile-process sandbox | `docs/CONTAINED_CORE_PRODUCT.md:86` |
| the remote provider routes are offline-tested adapters, not evidence a live provider is available | `docs/MINILEV_PROVIDER_RUNTIME.md:76-77` |
| repeated-intent / idempotency collapse: parked, not claimed | `docs/LEVIATHAN_MINILEV_CONFORMANCE.md:82` |
| the ClaimGate→Lev consumption bridge: Lev has a noncanonical inbox memo, not a producer, schema, CLI or consumer | `docs/CONTAINED_CORE_PRODUCT.md:87` |

### Three gaps worth naming

1. No durable Mini-Lev receipt is checked in. A repo-wide grep for `mini-levos-receipt`, `leviathan-minilev-conformance` and `leviathan-dry-run-comparison` outside `dist/` returns nothing. Every Mini-Lev receipt produced during the read was ephemeral. There is no retained evidence that the external Lev dry-run comparison has ever been executed.
2. The dist artifacts are stale. All three release sets are dated 2026-07-31. The r5 ZIP carries `mini_levos.py`, `mini_lev_topology.py`, `proposal_minilev_flow.py` and `execution_lease.py`, but not `integrated_minilev.py`, not `leviathan_reference.py`, not `_provider_harness/`, and not the two Mini-Lev docs. The shipped receipt has 14 command records; `scripts/verify_contained_core_bundle.py` now defines 26 labels. `docs/MINILEV_PROVIDER_RUNTIME.md:11` says the provider harness "is carried in the CB source package" — true of the working tree, false of every artifact in `dist/`.
3. The Lev conformance observer is brittle by design and unpinned. `observe_lev_exec_validate_flow` (`leviathan_reference.py:238-338`) parses the Lev YAML with 13 indentation-sensitive regexes. It records the observed sha256 but never compares it to an expected value. It passes today with zero failed checks. Any reformatting on the Lev side silently flips conformance to BLOCKED, and a shape change is indistinguishable from a content change.

## 3. ClaimGate ingestion

### The shape of it

CB never reads ClaimGate's ledgers, receipts, or result files. It ingests ClaimGate by executing it, and trusts only exit codes and stdout that it independently re-derives.

| Direction | Mechanism | Entry point |
|---|---|---|
| CB runs ClaimGate's chain | subprocess to `claim_verify.py` | `constraintbox gate <receipt.json>` |
| CB imports a ClaimGate module | `import claimgate_plugin.ratchet_floor_smt` | `constraintbox crosscheck` |
| CB runs the ratchet contract | subprocess to `run_ratchet_tick.py` | `constraintbox ratchet tick` |
| ClaimGate calls back into CB | registry-dispatched tier2 checker | `constraintbox admit-sim-evidence` |

### CB refuses to take ClaimGate's word

`_parse_chain_report` at `constraint_box/src/constraintbox/gate.py:114` is the clearest expression of "LLMs don't control their own gating" applied to ClaimGate itself. CB re-derives every summary field from the chain's own tier rows and refuses on contradiction:

- `verified_tiers` must equal the PASS rows, `unverified_tiers` the SKIP rows, `required_unmet` the non-PASS required rows (`:207-223`)
- `claim_verdicts` must equal the recomputed list (`:291`)
- a FAIL, ERROR or tamper report that is not REJECTED is refused (`:297`)
- a REJECTED report naming no failure is refused (`:299`)
- exit code and verdict string must agree via `CHAIN_VERDICTS_BY_EXIT` (`:37-41`, checked `:460`)
- duplicate JSON keys and NaN/Infinity are rejected (`:75`, `:84`)

Three channels — exit code, verdict string, tier rows — must independently agree, or the disposition becomes EVALUATION_ERROR.

Dispositions and process exit codes: ADMITTED 0, REFUSED 1, GateError 2, INSUFFICIENT_DEPTH 3, PARKED 4, EVALUATION_ERROR 5.

### The producer cannot name its own claim

`CLAIM_KIND_POLICY` at `constraint_box/src/constraintbox/simrun.py:40` is a CB-owned table. Any claim_kind the sim asserts in stdout or in created artifacts is scraped and parked in a separate `sim_asserted_claim_kind` field with a `claim_kind_conflict` boolean (`:213`).

### What is not ingested

This is the important negative. No CB-authored code reads:

- `claimgate_plugin/results/gate_ledger.jsonl` or `gate_ledger.head.json`
- the bypass, typed-grammar, numpy-containment or legacy-ratchet regression JSONs
- `claimgate_plugin/formal/ClaimGateChain.tla`, `chain_bmc_z3.py`, `chain_bmc_cvc5.py` — zero references from CB; `constraint_box/config/tla/ConstraintBox.tla` is a separate unrelated model
- ClaimGate fixtures, except as inputs when the chain itself runs

Gates and checkers are ingested as behaviour. Ledgers, receipts, results and proofs are ingested as nothing. A consequence: CB has no cross-run memory of ClaimGate decisions and cannot detect a verdict that changed between runs.

### The two-ClaimGate split

`constraint_box/claimgate_plugin/` is a full non-symlink copy of the root plugin, taken 2026-07-26 from commit `9ec613f77`, gitignored at `.gitignore:43`. `COPY_STATUS.md:45-50` declares a drift digest and the rule: if they diverge, re-copy rather than edit both. They have diverged.

| | repo root `claimgate_plugin/` | `constraint_box/claimgate_plugin/` |
|---|---|---|
| files | 534 | 427 |
| `ratchet_floor_smt.py` | present | absent |
| `verify_cb_sim_admission.py` | absent | present |
| `constraintbox_sim_evidence_v1` in registry | absent (31 lines) | present (37 lines) |
| `slop_gate.py`, `run_slop_regression.py`, `ci_slop_report.py` | present | absent |
| `canfail_smt.py`, `producer_standing.py`, `run_all_gates.py`, `evals/`, `tests/` | present | absent |

And CB binds both at once. `gate.py` resolves `package_root = parents[2] = constraint_box/`, so `constraintbox gate` runs the contained copy. `crosscheck.py:68` inserts `parents[3]` — the repo root — on `sys.path`, so `constraintbox crosscheck` imports the root copy. One package, two authorities, diverged.

Standalone-ness is split down the middle as a result. `ratchet_floor_smt.py` exists only at root, so the crosscheck lane cannot resolve from a standalone extraction. `verify_cb_sim_admission.py` and the `constraintbox_sim_evidence_v1` registry entry exist only in the copy, so `admit-sim-evidence` cannot work against repo-root ClaimGate.

### Doc-vs-code discrepancies found

1. `PROVENANCE.md:20-22` says "The ClaimGate implementation itself stays where it is… This directory does not copy it." False since 2026-07-26. `PROVENANCE.md:319` later records the duplicate as "real, open, widening". The file contradicts itself; line 20 is stale.
2. `PROVENANCE.md:313` says the mission case has no test and `test_gate_standalone.py` asserts the PARK path. Now false in CB's favour. `tests/test_gate_standalone.py:14` asserts ADMITTED (`:53`), `chain_root_inside_box` true (`:55`) and the box's own `claimgate.mjs` as tier0 (`:58`). It landed at commit `5378aeb6d`. Here the doc understates the code.
3. `gate.py:324` writes `"chain": CHAIN_RELATIVE_PATH` — a module constant, not the chain that actually ran. A `--chain` injection leaves no trace in the receipt. `PROVENANCE.md:326` records this as real and open.
4. Tier2 and tier3 are structurally unreachable, not merely unused. `PROVENANCE.md:314` records that both registered gates point at `system_v8/` paths outside the box and no fixture carries claim_kind `manifold_sim` or `quantum_claim`. They SKIP on every run — unmeasured, not broken.
5. `gate_registry.json:35` states in its own text that the registry, sealed decks and `evalcheck.mjs` do not live on a path the producing agent cannot write. External policy is tamper-detectable, not tamper-proof. This is self-declared, not derived.

### Evidence rung

Seven test modules run with the project interpreter: 42 passed, 26 subtests, 3.74 s, `git status --porcelain` byte-identical before and after. Rung: passes local rerun. Note `constraintbox` is not installed in the project env — the suite only imports with `PYTHONPATH=src`.

## 4. Wizard waves and nested LLM councils

### The owner canon

`OWNER_RULINGS_VERBATIM_20260806.md:131-144` and `:285-313` state the nesting: a WAVE is a set of LLM councils, a council's MEMBERS ARE THEMSELVES COUNCILS, and the third layer is actual skills and formal agents, all loaded with different MMMs and constrained inputs. The owner's arithmetic: "3 councils with 3 councils is actually not 9!!! it is 9 times all the skills, voices, tools, selected… 3-5 x 3-5 x 3-9". Waves loop on themselves and on each other. A loop without a receipt that advances nothing is dead. What each council does is arbitrary — the harness is content-agnostic.

### Three wave vocabularies, never to be merged

| Vocabulary | Where | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| Decision → Failure → Follow-Up | `~/wiki/wizard/packet-v4-3-current/WIZARD_v4_3.md:489-499` | the Wizard's three sequential council waves, nine parent routes total |
| W-INDEX, W-INDUCTION, W-DEDUCTION, W-PROMPT, W-OUTPUT, W-CONTEXT, W-PROJECT, W-REPAIR, W-VERIFY, plus W-WATCH | `constraint_box/config/member_role_wave_v1.json:6` | a CB-side member × role × wave registry. No driver. It is a registry, not a runtime. |
| W-PROMPT/W-COUNCIL/W-GATE/W-VERIFY/W-AUTORESEARCH, and W0–W4 | inside `cb_run.py` and `cb_integrated_run.py` | code-level phase names inside single scripts. Not councils. |

### What is built

Exactly one branch: the Failure council's falsifier route, in three generations, plus one skill member.

| Build | Path | What it did | Receipt |
|---|---|---|---|
| falsifier v1 | `cb_wave_falsifier.py:36-65` | 4 children × 2 disjoint subquestions; L3 8/8, L2 4/4, all admitted, verdict OPEN | `receipts/falsifier_20260807T163106Z/` |
| falsifier v2 | `cb_wave_falsifier_v2.py:35-53` | 4 children × 5 members on the same question under different sub-slices; 20/20 completed, all four councils DIVERGENT, round 2 fired for all four, 0 collapsed | `receipts/falsifier2_20260807T164600Z/` |
| falsifier v3 | `cb_wave_falsifier_v3.py:36-106` | deterministic members (rustworkx, z3, portion, celpy, icontract) vote inside the council and outrank any contradicting voice; multi-provider lanes; both design targets KILLED | three receipts, `falsifier3_20260807T17{0755,1222,1403}Z` |
| skill.premortem | `cb_skill_premortem.py:56-114` | executes the SKILL.md procedure rather than pasting it; 10 reasons, 10/10 dives conforming, 5/5 synthesis sections | `receipts/premortem_20260807T162555Z/` |
| flat voice councils | `cb_run.py`, `cb_run2.py` | 5 voices 4 admitted; 6 voices 6 admitted with four file-backed legs each | `cbrun_…153231Z`, `cbrun2_…153647Z` |

### Three claims in the docs and receipts that do not survive reading the code

1. `never_run = 0` across 131 members, present in all three `integrated_run` receipts, is a text-presence measure, not execution. The code now says so at `cb_integrated_run.py:90-96`: "member id absent from corpus text; NOT whether it ran". The real number is at `PROJECT_STATE.md:43` — 21 of 43 member × role × wave units EXEMPLIFIED.
2. The v3 falsifier's KILLED verdicts are structurally guaranteed. `'councils_run': 0` is a literal at `cb_wave_falsifier_v3.py:132` and `:144`, and the celpy rule requires `councils_run == councils_declared`. The wave has no SURVIVED branch. And it is not the only hardcode: z3 at `:61-66` tests 3 children × 4 members against a floor of 3 × 5, so 12 ≥ 15 is unsat for the decision target regardless of `councils_run`. Fixing one hardcode leaves that target killed by the other.
3. Conformance never reached the packet's own bar — 5 to 10 accepted child receipts per counted parent across a Codex/Opus/Sonnet/Haiku/Gemini family matrix. The best nested run, v2, hit exactly 5 per child on one family, because `dispatch()` defaults to `model='haiku'` (`cb_run.py:98`) and no falsifier call overrides it. Multi-family lanes exist only in v3, which is flat. On the packet's own honesty ladder that is REAL_ATTEMPT_PARTIAL at best. No run in the repo claims a label at all.

### Zhuangzi

`CB_BIAS_AND_DIVERSITY_MEASURE_20260806.md:71-87` and `OWNER_RULINGS_VERBATIM_20260806.md:171-172` both say zhuangzi operates one level up — it manufactures the dissimilar root inputs other members receive, rather than voting inside a council. In code it is one entry in `VOICE_MMM` at `cb_run.py:40` and a name in the default `--voices` lists. It is seated as an ordinary council member, the exact role the ruling says it is not. `member_role_wave_v1.json:9` records the generator role as NEVER_RUN. The divergence organ is unexercised.

## 5. The deterministic gate and the Python library estate

### The gate itself

`run_gate` at `constraint_box/src/constraintbox/gate.py:387`, reached by `constraintbox gate <receipt.json>` (parser at `cli.py:364`, dispatch at `cli.py:1229`). A receipt path goes in, a fixed non-LLM chain checks it against policy the producer cannot write, and one of five dispositions plus a matching process exit code comes out. `promotion_allowed: false` is hardcoded at `gate.py:348`.

A separate standalone enforcer, `claimgate_plugin/three_engine_seal.py`, is not called by `run_gate`. It re-derives instead of trusting:

- rule R1 (`:107-109`) hard-rejects numpy, scipy or mpmath labelled `load_bearing`
- at least two authoritative engines must each carry a `load_bearing` label and a numeric value (`:142-146`)
- they must agree on the same metric id within 1e-6 (`:150-166`)
- the jax leg must re-run and reproduce to 1e-9 (`:73-98`, `:174-181`)
- an unreadable receipt fails closed (`:190`)

### The two library estates

CB-light is what the gate itself needs. `pyproject.toml` declares exactly five runtime dependencies:

| Library | Kernel role | Site |
|---|---|---|
| z3-solver | SMT decision on the typed request gate; SAT admits, UNSAT parks | `constraints.py:186` |
| cvc5 | independent second decider over the same encoding; the pair yields AGREE or UNRESOLVED, never a single-solver truth claim | `dualsolve.py:212` |
| sympy | exact rational normalization for one controller-built polynomial over QQ | `symbolic.py:823` |
| rustworkx | DAG check, topological order, reachability, and the M01a topology preflight | `graph_topology_worker.py:130` |
| maude==1.6.0 | one bounded controller-defined rewrite inside an isolated worker | `maude_rewrite.py:230` |

numpy is an optional `numeric` extra and never a decider. hypothesis is a `test` extra with zero imports under `src/`.

CB-heavy is the external sim estate — S1 through S4 tiers in `docs/02_SIM_SETUP_TIERS.md`, from stdlib/scipy up to JAX, Julia, Quimb, PySINDy, torch and CUDA. The split is enforced by role, not by import guard. `docs/CAPABILITY_EXECUTION_MATRIX.md:36-38` labels every engine `EXTERNAL_NOT_CB_KERNEL`: engine output "cannot choose a gate, transition, retry, release, promotion, or claim ceiling".

### The paired accept-and-refuse pattern

Stated at `cb_light_integrations.py:4-6`: "a gate that has only ever passed has not been exemplified." Every wired library gets a conformant input it must admit and a deliberately broken twin it must refuse, in the same self-test. Exit 0 only when the two counts match.

Nineteen more libraries are exemplified this way across two script modules:

| Module | Libraries |
|---|---|

### The eight control laws

`scripts/cb_control_laws.py` declares eight laws in its docstring. Three have executable checks.

| Law | Statement | Code |
|---|---|---|
| 1 divergence collapse | a destructive step inside a divergence loop annihilates the basin set | `check_divergence_loop`, `:122`, asserted `:147-149` |
| 2 conserved stratum | the strategy-memory stage conserves one stratum exactly while the rest contracts | `check_conserved_stratum`, `:130`, asserted `:152` |
| 3 fixed-point reference | monotone convergence is measured against the composed word's own fixed point | `true_fixed_point` `:90` + `monotone_fraction` `:107`, both arms asserted |
| 4 surface learning | learning is deformation of the registry, not motion of run states | prose only |
| 5 input diversity is measurable | shared root inputs collapse a swarm | prose only |
| 6 member subsumption and dead votes | more members can make a council worse | prose only here; seat machinery at `cb_all_tools_council.py:261-287` |
| 7 shared precompute | exhaustive deterministic deployment is only free above a shared index | prose only; design at `cb_integrated_run.py:6` |
| 8 live loop | an iteration is live only if it emitted a receipt and its declared measure moved | prose only here; enforced in `cb_loop.py:56-64` |

## 6. How it all runs together — the chain and the commands

### The two chains

```
CHAIN A — the packaged product (constraintbox CLI)
  constraintbox formal run  -> formal_flow.py -> MiniLevRuntime -> hash-chained ledger -> receipt
  constraintbox gate        -> gate.py -> subprocess claim_verify.py (contained copy) -> disposition + exit code
  constraintbox crosscheck  -> import claimgate_plugin.ratchet_floor_smt (ROOT copy) -> two deciders
  constraintbox ratchet tick-> subprocess ratchet_contract/run_ratchet_tick.py -> results diff
  constraintbox admit-sim-evidence -> writes claim -> run_gate -> tier2 -> back into constraintbox.sim_admission
  constraintbox request     -> compile_user_profile (6 MMM packs) -> boxrun -> agentrun prompt

CHAIN B — the swarm scripts (nothing here imports Chain A)
  cb_loop.py --cycles N
    :45 -> cb_integrated_run.py           [free, offline]
              :163 -> cb_control_laws.py --self-test
    :93 -> cb_wave_falsifier_v3.py        [*** NETWORK + BILLED ***]
              :28 imports cb_multi_provider.fanout
              :169 -> fanout()
                       urlopen https://openrouter.ai            [free tier, key from env]
                       subprocess `claude -p --model haiku`     [*** BILLED ***]
                       subprocess `codex exec`   [--lanes only]
                       subprocess `gemini -p`    [--lanes only]
    :97 -> cb_autoresearch_loop.py        [free, offline]

  Second billing path, NOT reachable from cb_loop:
  cb_run.py:101 -> ~/.codex/skills/claude-bridge/scripts/claude_child_fanout.py -> claude children
    imported by cb_run2.py, cb_skill_premortem.py, cb_wave_falsifier.py, cb_wave_falsifier_v2.py

  Called by nothing: cb_tiered_dispatch.py, cb_lateral_wave.py, cb_lateral_heavy.py, cb_all_tools_council.py
```

### The one nested council path that executes end to end

`cb_wave_falsifier_v2.py`, in order:

1. `StrategyMemory` seals `prompt_intent`, `success_condition` and `claim_ceiling` as a conserved stratum.
2. `build_l3()` loads, per required child (voice.popper, voice.pushback, voice.feynman, guard.boundary_check), the agent spec at `.claude/agents/voice-<v>.md` plus the mini-MMM at `~/wiki/wizard/packet-v4-3-current/mmm/mini/full/voices/md/MMM_VOICE_<V>_FULL_v4_1.md`, then emits 5 jobs — one per sub-slice (literal, operational, adversarial, historical, boundary) — all asking that child's one question. 20 jobs.
3. `cb_run.dispatch()` writes `jobs.json`, subprocesses `claude_child_fanout.py` at `--timeout-sec 150 --max-concurrency 4 --global-max-active 8`, reads `fanout_receipt.json`, and counts only children whose status is `completed`. That count law is code, at `cb_run.py:107-113`.
4. `collapse_check()` per child: pairwise `SequenceMatcher` over the 5 answers. Identical or mean ≥ 0.85 is COLLAPSED, ≥ 0.55 CONVERGENT, else DIVERGENT.
5. A debate round 2 fires only for DIVERGENT children.
6. A deterministic tally sets the route verdict. KILLED at ≥ 2 killed, SURVIVED only if all survived, else OPEN. No model decides it.
7. Receipt written with `promotion_allowed` false.

### The current state of the loop driver

`PROJECT_STATE.md:69` says do not run `cb_loop.py`. Here is what a reader found underneath that instruction.

- `cb_loop_state.json` records exactly 2 cycles, both on 2026-08-07. Cycle 1 advanced. Cycle 2 was STATIC — no declared measure moved. `autoresearch_wrote` is false in both.
- Leg 3, `cb_autoresearch_loop.py`, has never executed successfully. `cb_autoresearch_loop.py:73` does `set(params['ladder'])` and raises KeyError. Two scripts write `config/cb_tuned_params.json` under incompatible schemas.
- No return code is ever checked. `cb_loop.py:31` records `rc` but `advanced()` at `:56-64` ignores it; the falsifier's rc is discarded at `:93-95`; the autoresearch leg is judged only by the string "WROTE BACK" in stdout. A crashing leg is indistinguishable from a working one.

- `--max-usd` appears in the usage docstring at `cb_loop.py:15` but is not an argparse option at `:68-72`. The documented command fails with "unrecognized arguments". Still missing.
- The only cost cap in the entire chain is `--budget 1` per child at `cb_run.py:103`, and it lives inside the external fanout script, not in CB.
- A total dispatch failure is reported as success. `cb_run.py:101-105` discards the subprocess result with no returncode check, so `res={}`, `spawned=0`, the count law `0 <= 0` holds, W-GATE is empty, and main returns 0 with a receipt describing a clean run.

Both readings are consistent with the evidence if the file was edited after the last successful run. The consequence matters: if the census leg exits non-zero, no MEASURES line is printed, `advanced()` is always STATIC, and the loop burns exactly `--dead-cycles-allowed` cycles of billed falsifier calls before stopping. Nobody knows who made that edit, and it is untracked, so there is no diff to review.

### 2. Is the 23/23 all-tools council result strong or is it a fixture artifact?

Reader 4 calls it the strongest-evidenced layer of the whole subsystem: 23 members in "earn", 0 blind, 0 errored, two receipts.

Reader 5 says the clean sweep cannot distinguish a library with a distinctive power from one that only re-reads a shared boolean. The BAD twin differs from GOOD on seven fields at once, and eight members — blake3, xxhash, rfc8785, zstandard, lmdb, maude, deepdiff, and partly pygit2 — reduce to `d.get('promotion_allowed') is False` after a library call whose result is always true. Recorded at `cb_control_laws.py:40-41` and `config/member_role_wave_v1.json:35` for 9 voice prompts. A reader transcribed `cb_run.py:74-95` verbatim and ran it over all nine `VOICE_MMM` slices: max_overlap 0.0, not 0.368.

`CB_BIAS_AND_DIVERSITY_MEASURE_20260806.md:54` says measure the shared leading prefix. `cb_run.py:75-81` argues the opposite — that the preamble is a conserved stratum under LAW 2, and scoring it makes the strategy manager and the diversity gate fight each other.

The docs say mini-MMMs shape salience. `cb_run.py:36` uses a hardcoded 9-entry dict of one-line strings and opens no MMM file. `cb_run2.py` composes four hashed file legs instead.

Two readings: the inline dict is a deliberately cheap v1 lane, or it is drift that `cb_run2.py` was written to correct. Neither has been excluded.

### 6. Is the two-product split intended?

Reader 2 asks whether MiniLevOS gating the CLI surface but not the swarm loop is intended — two separate products — or is the gap. Reader 6 confirms the split independently from the script side. Nobody found a document that rules on it.

## Unresolved, and worth an owner decision

Ordered by how much rests on the answer.

1. Which ClaimGate is canonical? `gate.py` binds the contained copy; `crosscheck.py` binds the root copy; they have diverged. `PROVENANCE.md:370` already lists this as an open owner action. Until it is settled, "the gate" names two code paths.
2. Is `input_diversity_gate.py` recoverable? `SESSION_SAVE_20260807.md:64` names `CB_CONTROL_PACK_20260806_v4.zip` as the container. If it is lost, every measurement attributed to it — and to the other eight named members — is uncorroborated in this repo, and `member_role_wave_v1.json:35` carries status EXEMPLIFIED for a module with no bytes.
3. Should the `cb_*` chain be committed? Nothing in the swarm subsystem is in git.
4. Which script owns `config/cb_tuned_params.json`? Until one owns it, the autoresearch leg stays dead.
5. Is the falsifier's LLM fanout meant to be advisory only? As written it fires after the deterministic verdict is fixed, and the provider-diversity and collapse audits are computed, stored, then excluded from the verdict. A FAKE_SWARM audit still yields OPEN. Ten calls per cycle, of which two are billed, are pure cost.
6. Can the v3 falsifier ever return SURVIVED? Not while `'councils_run': 0` is a literal at `:132` and `:144` — and even then, the z3 member's 12 ≥ 15 test kills the decision target independently.
7. Should `gate_registry.json`'s trust root move to a producer-unwritable path? The file says at `:35` that it has not. Everything downstream of the registry inherits that answer.
8. Should a declared registry member with no importable module be a hard failure? At present a row can claim EXEMPLIFIED forever and nothing checks it.
9. Should the dist artifacts be re-cut? They ship 14 verification commands against a current suite of 26, and omit the conformance harness, the provider harness and both Mini-Lev docs.
10. Should the handoff builder stop flattening nested receipt directories? `cb_build_handoff.py:95-101` globs `receipts/**/*.json` and copies to `d / src.name`, so identical basenames overwrite. The shipped `MANIFEST.json` has 218 entries with 7 duplicate paths — 29 entries collapse onto 7 files, so 22 receipts were lost and the manifest disagrees with its own directory.
11. Should `PROJECT_STATE.md`'s defect detectors move to tests that fail when the defect is present? Two of them cannot observe their own fixes. `cb_project_state.py:79` inspects the 400 characters before the EXT_ALL line, and the repair was added after that line, so defect 5 is reported forever. `:82-84` greps historical receipts for a literal string, so defect 6 persists until those receipts are deleted.
12. Do `cb_run2.py`'s character caps (2200 / 2600 / 2200 / 1800 per leg) truncate any leg? Where a file exceeds its cap, the model saw truncated bytes while the receipt records the sha256 of the full file. The receipt hash does not identify what the model read. Nobody has measured how many legs truncate.
13. Is a six-word MMM slice enough variable stratum to gate on? With 2-shingle sets the Jaccard metric can take essentially only 0, 1/3 and 1, so the 0.8 threshold never binds in the middle. In `cb_run.py` the diversity gate is a near-duplicate detector on a one-line string, not a graded measure. The `cb_run2.py` variant, scoring long agent-spec text, is genuinely graded — 0.3207 max, 0.2698 mean in its live receipt.
14. Should the gate's bounds be written into the receipt? The doc promises re-judgement without re-running; `cb_run.py:95` hard-codes 0.8 and dup==0. A threshold change would silently reclassify past receipts.
15. Does `provider_diversity` need a minimum-liveness floor? It requires only two distinct families and mean similarity under 0.75. Receipt `falsifier3_20260807T170755Z` certifies REAL_SWARM from 2 of 5 lanes live. Two responses currently certify a swarm.
16. Nesting and provider diversity have never been combined. v2 nests three layers but every one of its 20 children was haiku. v3 spans two families but is flat. The owner's stated anti-collapse mechanism — different MMMs and different base models at the leaves — has never run in one wave.
17. Which member count is the target? The two registries hold 131 ids; the Integration Wave Program says 137. `cb_project_state.py:127` hardcodes the string "131 = the union of the two member registries" inside a generator whose stated premise at `:105-106` is that nothing is typed from memory. 72 + 59 happens to equal 131 today; the line does not recompute.
18. Is `manager.strategy_memory` run or not? `member_role_wave_v1.json:44` says NEVER_RUN while `cb_strategy_memory.py` runs inside every wave script. Either the registry is stale, or RUN means something stricter than the receipts show — and the same registry is the evidence base for the 21/43 execution number.
19. Should the receipt key `controller_base_mmm_not_prompt_context` (`agentrun.py:955`) be renamed? It is accurate about agentrun's own second copy of the packs, but a reader auditing receipts would conclude the packs never reach the model. They do, through `boxrun.context_text`.
